issues.description: The Genre struct in the solution declares its 'name' property as 'private let name: String' while Client.main() (in a different source file) accesses genre.name. In Swift, 'private' restricts access to the declaring file, so the Client code cannot access name and this causes a compilation error. The problem statement describes Genre as having a name (no private restriction), so the visibility in the solution is inconsistent with the intended usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Genre.name property accessible to the Client by removing the 'private' modifier (use 'let name: String' so it has module-internal access) or change it to 'public let name: String' if broader visibility is desired. Alternatively, provide a public accessor method. Ensure the property's visibility matches how Client.main() uses genre.name.
